title: The Directory That Answered
description:
Tunde drops three log files on the desk. 'The Griot did not guess the admin path — they fuzzed it and the server answered. Everything is in these tabs, but the interesting line is never where you expect it. More than one source IP touches /legacy-admin — only one of them is the attacker. The ffuf tab has tokens planted to mislead a careless analyst. Trust the BEHAVIOUR — user-agent, what was actually retrieved, and the order — over any banner or <- HIGH VALUE label.'

Amaka: 'Name the attacker IP, the one path whose retrieval changed the outcome of the breach, and the path that is interesting but not load-bearing. The naive call — first IP to hit /legacy-admin is the attacker — is wrong here, and so is trusting the inline TRAN tokens on the ffuf tab. The HTTP access log runs long; pay attention to the source address, the timestamps, and what the server actually returned. Evidence over banners.'

In the pentest finding (task 9) you will name which exposed path actually changed the outcome of the breach, and which one is interesting but not load-bearing.

Reference: MITRE ATT&CK T1083 File and Directory Discovery; OWASP Top 10 2021 A05 Security Misconfiguration; CWE-538 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory).

widgetConfig.instructions: Three log tabs. The flag is in one of them — buried, and only on one line. The other two tabs are needed to know WHICH line. Read carefully.
